rules.sentence: The treatment of osteosarcoma typically requires some combination of wide excision, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy.
Localized high-grade osteosarcomas are treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy, radical surgical resection, and adjuvant chemotherapy.[6]
Approximately 10% to 20% of patients with osteosarcoma have evidence of metastases at their initial presentation; the most common metastatic site is the lungs.[7]
With the routine use of chemotherapy, approximately two-thirds of children and adolescents with osteosarcoma will achieve long-term cures.
